presentations.abstract: Understanding and forecasting lake dynamics is essential for monitoring water quality and ecosystem health in lakes and reservoirs. While machine learning models trained on ecological time-series data have shown promise, they are typically task-specific, often designed for a single lake or variable, and struggle to generalize across diverse aquatic environments. Recent time-series foundation models (TSFMs) offer cross-domain generalization but fall short in ecological contexts. To address these limitations, we introduce LakeFM, a foundation model for aquatic ecosystems, pre-trained on multi-variable, multi-depth data from both simulated and real-world lakes. LakeFM flattens spatiotemporal ecological signals into token sequences. Our experiments demonstrate two key findings: 1. Zero-shot generalization - LakeFM consistently outperforms state-of-the-art TSFMs like Chronos and MOMENT on unseen lakes and variables. 2. Lake-level structure - Learned embeddings reveal latent clusters of lakes with similar ecological behaviour.

presentations.title: Investigating Timescale Variability in Lake Water Quality using Knowledge-Guided Machine Learning
presentations.abstract: High-frequency observations of lake water quality variables, such as dissolved oxygen and chlorophyll and phycocyanin fluorescence, show sub-daily fluctuations that may be important to emergent water quality phenomena. Knowledge-guided machine learning (KGML) offers a hybrid model alternative that integrates both theory and data, linking traditional limnological knowledge with modern AI technologies. Here we evaluate how sub-daily processes influence lake water quality and examine the extent to which different modeling approaches reproduce these high-frequency dynamics. We compare predictions from a one-dimensional PB model, a ML-only model trained solely on observed data, and a hybrid KGML model that incorporates PB model outputs into the ML learning process. Models are trained, validated, and tested using multi-year high-frequency datasets from Lake Mendota (WI, USA).

presentations.title: Application of machine learning calibration to improve surface water quality modelling of Lake Erie
presentations.abstract: Process-based coupled hydrodynamic-biogeochemical models are essential tools for assessing lake water quality and their calibration is often subjective, labour-intensive, and computationally expensive. In this work, we develop a hybrid surrogate-based machine learning (ML) and genetic algorithm (GA) framework to assess and calibrate a three-dimensional AEM3D water quality model of Lake Erie. The ML surrogate is trained to regress the model parameter space onto the discrepancy between simulated and observed water quality variables. The GA then operates on this surrogate to efficiently search the high-dimensional parameter space to identify parameter sets that minimise the model-observation discrepancy.

presentations.title: A Hurdle-Model Framework to Explain Interannual Variability in Lake Habitat Conditions
presentations.abstract: Linking spatially extensive, long-term, datasets of lake profile measurements, local and global climate data, and lake characteristics is necessary when investigating interannual variability in habitat conditions. Coldwater fish species residing in these historically habitable lakes face increasing risks. We leveraged an extensive dataset of lake profiles compiled by members of the Midwest Glacial Lakes Partnership Science & Data Team to calculate an oxythermal habitat metric (vertical habitat thickness) across time for hundreds of Minnesota lakes. A hurdle model, combining a binomial stage and linear mixed effects stage, was used to identify drivers and interannual controls of summertime oxythermal fish habitat across lake types.

presentations.title: NOISY NEIGHBORS: LAKES THAT ARE CLOSE TOGETHER MAY HAVE VERY DIFFERENT ENVIRONMENTS
presentations.abstract: Lakes are sentinels of environmental change, integrating impacts of changes occurring in the atmosphere and watershed around them. Here, we used data from over 1,200 lakes in the Adirondack State Park (New York, USA) to assess the variability and similarity of lakes through time and space. Despite an enormous range in lake attributes, we identified ten clusters of lake types. There was a small but significant correlation between geographic and environmental similarity, however there is substantial variability in this relationship. The correlations between environmental similarity and either morphometric or watershed similarity were very weak.

presentations.title: Harnessing Machine Learning and Satellite Remote Sensing to Assess the Impact of Best Management Practices in Water Quality
presentations.affiliation: University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science
presentations.abstract: Highly resolved water quality measurements are needed to better evaluate the efficacy of Best Management Practices (BMPs) and support decision-making tools. Here, we leverage machine learning (ML) and publicly available data to generate and analyze measurements of nutrient pollution and water clarity throughout Choptank River, the major tributary of Chesapeake Bay, USA. This presentation describes a Python-based mixture density network for robust and explainable retrieval of total nitrogen, total phosphorus, and water transparency. Performance is evaluated using mean absolute error and bias, and the best model is interpreted with Shapley Additive Explanations and an attention mechanism.

title: The Next Frontier in Aquatic Sciences: Linking Remote Sensing, Data Science, Modeling, and Open Science to Better Understand Aquatic Ecosystems

presentations.title: FROM ECHOES TO ESTIMATES: MAPPING AND PREDICTING SUBMERGED MACROPHYTE BIOMASS IN A TROPICAL RESERVOIR
presentations.affiliation: Federal University of Latin American Integration
presentations.abstract: Submerged aquatic macrophytes play essential roles in lentic ecosystems, reflecting environmental quality and serving as effective bioindicators. This project evaluates the influence of seasonality and environmental quality on macrophyte biomass, species richness, and abundance in the Itaipu Reservoir, a strategic binational system. We integrate hydroacoustic data with water and sediment quality measurements and plant biomass. Preliminary results show no effect of depth (up to 4 m) or seasonality on biomass. A Gamma GLM revealed a significant relationship between hydroacoustic plant height and biomass.

presentations.title: HIERARCHICAL ECO-ZONE DELINEATION IN DATA-SCARCE AFROTROPICAL RIVER LANDSCAPES USING OPEN DATA MODELLING FRAMEWORKS
presentations.affiliation: University of Natural resources and life Sciences
presentations.abstract: Understanding spatial ecological heterogeneity is critical for modelling and managing aquatic ecosystems, yet most Afrotropical environmental classifications remain limited to drainage divides or coarse expert-based schemes. Here, we integrated global remote sensing datasets, open environmental data, and multiple machine-learning algorithms within an open-source workflow to delineate hierarchical eco-zones for Uganda's lake, riverine, and wetland landscapes. The workflow produced four nested eco-regional maps, with five major ecoregions at the broadest level and 3 finer bioregional subdivisions.

presentations.title: Integrating modeling, remote sensing and in-situ data to characterize hydro-sedimentological dynamics and climate impacts in the Río de la Plata estuary
presentations.abstract: This work synthesizes a long-term effort to characterize the Río de la Plata, a large microtidal estuary where sediment-rich waters from the Paraná and Uruguay rivers mix with shelf waters. Over recent decades, we combined high-resolution 3D numerical modeling, continuous in-situ monitoring, and remote sensing to investigate governing physical processes. Initial research evolved from nested models capturing tide-surge interactions to fully coupled wave-current-sediment simulations incorporating self-weight consolidation. Processing satellite imagery spanning two decades revealed the complex spatio-temporal dynamics of the turbidity front.

presentations.title: INFERRING MULTITROPHIC CARBON DYNAMICS IN THE BERMUDA ATLANTIC TIME-SERIES STUDY USING A MECHANISTIC ECOSYSTEM MODEL
presentations.abstract: Modern sampling and analysis tools generate extensive high-resolution data on microbial communities. To address this gap, we integrated four years of data from the Bermuda Atlantic Time-series Study (BATS) into FluxNet, a mechanistic ecosystem model that estimates carbon fluxes among species and trophic compartments. The model represents approximately forty of the most abundant taxa across heterotrophic bacteria, phytoplankton, heterotrophic protists, and zooplankton, as well as particulate and dissolved organic matter, and reconstructs interaction networks by constraining carbon transfer in a mass-balanced framework.

presentations.title: ASSESSING IMPACTS OF SEA-LEVEL RISE ON ALBEMARLE-PAMLICO SOUND, NORTH CAROLINA: FOUNDATIONS FOR ECOLOGICAL IMPLICATIONS
presentations.abstract: The Albemarle-Pamlico Sound (APS) lagoonal estuary in northeastern North Carolina is the second largest estuarine system in the United States. To investigate hydrodynamic responses to these changes, a hindcast simulation for 2019 was developed using Semi-Implicit Cross-Scale Hydrodynamic System Model (SCHISM) and validated with in-situ observations. We assessed the impacts of SLR by isolating changes in mean sea level (MSL) under two scenarios: a moderate SLR scenario (CMIP6 SSP370) and a high SLR scenario (SSP585). Model results indicate that MSL changes significantly influence seasonally varying conditions, with spatially heterogeneous impacts on hydrodynamic circulation, salt flux, stratification, and water quality parameters in APS.

presentations.title: Bioaccumulation and Subcellular Distribution of Metals Across Species through Quantitative Ion-Character Relationship Modelling
presentations.abstract: Metal contamination poses ecological risks to aquatic biota, especially when toxicological data are scarce and metals are not regulated. As metal toxicity is closely linked to their intracellular distribution, we developed Quantitative Ion Character-Activity Relationship (QICAR) models to predict metal bioaccumulation and subcellular compartmentalization. Our dataset included measurements for 34 metals across nine fish, one amphipod and one mammal, combined with 21 metal descriptors. Tree-based models exhibited the best predictive performance, with mean LOSO R² values ranging from 0.77 to 0.84 across endpoints.

title: The Next Frontier in Aquatic Sciences: Linking Remote Sensing, Data Science, Modeling, and Open Science to Better Understand Aquatic Ecosystems

presentations.title: Development of a three-dimensional model to manage a drinking water supply using open data and software
presentations.abstract: As part of the project 'Managing Events and Extremes in Water Supplies', we have set up the three-dimensional (3D) open-source pyGETM model for Mälaren, a large (>1000 km2) lake in Sweden that provides drinking water to over 2 million people. We worked in close collaboration with the local drinking water providers in designing meaningful scenarios. By using open data and open-source software, we aim to provide a blueprint for future applications elsewhere. We performed a study on PFAS release and transport in the lake. The results showed a marked spatial variation in the relative importance of the different PFAS sources and in the chance of exceeding drinking water limits.

presentations.title: INTEGRATING A HEAT-PUMP THERMAL EXCHANGE MODULE IN THE GENERAL LAKE MODEL (GLM)
presentations.abstract: Inland waters account for 3.6% of global land heat uptake, with natural lakes accounting for the majority of this uptake. These water bodies offer substantial potential for thermal energy systems that provide heating and cooling. Here, we present a new thermal use module integrated into the General Lake Model (GLM) framework. The module features: (1) depth-flexible heat extraction or injection at static or dynamic intake/outfall locations; (2) compatibility with both open-loop and closed-loop system configurations; (3) user-defined operational parameters; (4) seamless coupling with the Aquatic Ecodynamics (AED) library.

presentations.title: Coupled process-based modeling links catchment deforestation to temperate reservoir water quality: Unraveling indirect global change impacts
presentations.affiliation: Nanjing Institute of Geography and Limnology, Chinese Academy of Sciences
presentations.abstract: The next frontier in aquatic sciences hinges on integrating modeling and data science to disentangle direct and indirect global change drivers. We address this with a coupled modeling approach linking catchment-reservoir dynamics, focusing on a predam network feeding Germany's largest drinking water reservoir. We integrated process-based models (HYPE: catchment nutrient exports; GOTM-WET: reservoir dynamics) validated with multi-temporal deforestation-era datasets. We show that by 2035, extreme deforestation (80% loss) drives elevated catchment nutrient fluxes, transforming the mesotrophic reservoir to a eutrophic state.

presentations.title: DETECTING EARLY WARNING INDICATORS IN GLOBAL LAKE SYSTEMS USING A SATELLITE DATA AND LAKE MODELLING APPROACH
presentations.abstract: Freshwater ecosystems continue to show early signs of tipping behaviour globally, highlighting growing risks for the environment and society. Using the European Space Agency's Lake CCI dataset alongside ISIMIP3b global lake simulations, this study examines the emergence of tipping behaviour across multiple physical variables from the simulated historical period through the satellite era and into future climate scenarios.

presentations.title: LARGE-SCALE ASSESSMENT OF LAKE STABILITY USING CLIMATE-FILTERED SATELLITE TIME SERIES AND HYBRID STATISTICAL-AI CLASSIFICATION
presentations.abstract: Lakes provide crucial ecosystem services yet are increasingly exposed to rapid climate change and human pressures. To assess lake stability across large regions, we developed an early warning framework coupled with a scalable AI classifier using 40+ years of Landsat derived chlorophyll-a time series for thousands of lakes in the Lake Winnipeg Watershed. We trained a hybrid surrogate model that combines Random Forest predictors with a Transformer neural network.

presentations.title: LEVERAGING DEEP LEARNING TECHNIQUES AND CROSS-SCALE MODELING TO INFORM RESILIENT RIVER-COAST ADAPTATION STRATEGIES
presentations.abstract: Restoring river-coast connectivity requires tools that capture both fine-scale shoreline conditions and broader processes that govern hydrodynamics, sediment exchange, and habitat evolution. This study presents an integrated approach applied throughout tidal tributaries of the Chesapeake Bay system in the USA. Updated shoreline and intertidal habitat inventories derived from high-resolution imagery, combined with deep learning methods for automated shoreline structure identification, provide current and consistent information.

title: The Next Frontier in Aquatic Sciences: Linking Remote Sensing, Data Science, Modeling, and Open Science to Better Understand Aquatic Ecosystems

presentations.title: Temporal variation of harmful algal blooms in northern temperate lakes under a changing climate: A view from on the ground and outer space
presentations.abstract: How are harmful algal blooms (HABs) trending in response to rapid global warming? We analyzed in-situ bioindicators (chlorophyll a, cyanobacterial cell counts and microcystin concentration) of HABs across 107 cases from lakes monitored across central Alberta, Canada. Decadal trends were most often irregular and episodic rather than linear. Six lakes were selected for ground-truthing of a chlorophyll a retrieval algorithm based on Landsat satellite imagery data to reconstruct histories of HABs dating back to 1985. Spatiotemporal trends were largely unsynchronized among and within lakes.

presentations.title: Three-Dimensional Representation of Animal Motion in Six Degrees of Freedom
presentations.abstract: Animals change position in their surroundings for several reasons, including to forage, to find a mate, or to avoid predation. In this work, we take the perspective of the animal and examine the actions the animal takes with respect to the six degrees of freedom of motion. In doing this, we are able to describe animal motion in three dimensions and to simulate realistic trajectories for a particular planktonic crustacean in a laboratory setting.

presentations.title: CubeSat Observations of Phycocyanin and Chlorophyll-a in a Large, Regulated River
presentations.abstract: Cyanobacterial blooms in large, regulated rivers threaten human and ecosystem health. Here, we evaluate the efficacy of using the commercial Super Dove constellation from Planet Labs, combined with deep learning, to estimate concentrations of phycocyanin and chlorophyll-a in the Illinois River Basin, USA. Our results indicate that multitask neural networks improve predictive capability compared to single task models for both phycocyanin and chlorophyll-a. Our model will enable near daily mapping of phycocyanin and chlorophyll-a concentrations at ~3-meter resolution along rivers.

presentations.title: Algal Assemblages and Radiocarbon Dating-Based Reconstruction of Paleolimnological Conditions in the Yamuna River, Delhi
presentations.abstract: The Yamuna River, originating from the Yamunotri Glacier, flows 1,376 kilometers before merging with the Ganga. This study presents the first detailed paleolimnological investigation of the Yamuna, focusing on reconstructing prehistoric ecological conditions through sediment core analysis. A total of 31 diatom species were identified from 18 sediment samples. Radiocarbon (C-14) dating revealed ages ranging from 17,020 BC to 85 BC. Most samples belonged to the Holocene and Pleistocene epochs. Geochemical analyses identified elemental and mineral compositions, including heavy metals and oxides.

presentations.title: HARNESSING LONG-TERM SENSOR DATASETS AND INTERPRETABLE MACHINE LEARNING TO UNDERSTAND THE DRIVERS OF DEEP-WATER CYANOBACTERIAL BLOOMS
presentations.abstract: Long-term, high-resolution aquatic datasets analyzed with models and interpretable machine learning can reveal previously-overlooked dynamics in freshwater systems. We used a decade of vertically resolved, high-frequency sensor profiles of cyanobacterial concentrations from Beaverdam Reservoir (Virginia, USA), combined with chemistry and meteorological data to quantify interannual and within-season variability in cyanobacterial DCM magnitude and depth. We applied random forest models with explainable AI (SHapley Additive exPlanations) to identify and interpret predictors.

presentations.title: Harmful algal bloom detection and prediction system for the San Jose Lagoon
presentations.abstract: We present an integrated monitoring and forecasting system developed for the San José Lagoon in San Juan, Puerto Rico, combining satellite data, in-situ measurements, and machine learning techniques. Daily satellite data from the Sentinel-3 Ocean and Land Colour Instrument were automatically retrieved, quality filtered, and processed into spatially averaged chlorophyll fields for the lagoon. To forecast harmful algal blooms (HABs), we developed histogram-based gradient boosting regression and classification models. The regression models produced the most accurate 1-, 2-, and 3-week chlorophyll forecasts.

title: The Next Frontier in Aquatic Sciences: Linking Remote Sensing, Data Science, Modeling, and Open Science to Better Understand Aquatic Ecosystems

presentations.title: GLOBAL HYDROGRAPHY IN SUPPORT OF AQUATIC ECOLOGY: RECENT UPDATES TO THE HYDROSHEDS SUITE OF PRODUCTS
presentations.abstract: Since its introduction in 2008, the global HydroSHEDS data framework and its related products have transformed large-scale hydro-ecological research and applications worldwide by offering spatially standardized hydrographic information. HydroSHEDS and its suite of related products is currently undergoing a major upgrade based on a new underpinning digital elevation model (TanDEM-X) at 30 m spatial resolution. This presentation will describe key characteristics of the new products, including maps and databases of global river, lake and wetland distributions, lake mixing, river barriers and reservoirs, concentrations of emerging contaminants and other hydro-environmental attributes.

presentations.title: A regional remote sensing analysis of water level fluctuations' impact on littoral habitat in Intermountain West reservoirs.
presentations.abstract: Artificially formed lakes, or reservoirs, are a critical piece of infrastructure for the Intermountain West of the USA. Reservoirs provide water storage for hydropower, drinking, and irrigation while also supporting local economies through recreational use. In this work, we synthesized multiple readily available data sources including lake bathymetry, reservoir storage, and satellite remote sensing, to estimate changes in littoral habitat extent and water clarity across a gradient of Intermountain West reservoirs and lakes. Using Secchi disk depth modeled from Landsat imagery we were able to calculate the euphotic depth across each reservoir's surface, throughout the available timeseries (1984-2024).

presentations.title: ASSESSING THE TRANSFERABILITY OF MACROPHYTE REMOTE SENSING MODELS IN THE OPTICALLY COMPLEX FLUVIAL ST. LAWRENCE RIVER, CANADA
presentations.abstract: Earth observation (EO) creates important opportunities for the high-resolution monitoring of macrophyte ecosystems, yet inland waters still lack operational products. We evaluate the transferability of EO-based macrophyte detection models across contrasting environmental conditions in the fluvial St. Lawrence River (Canada), with the goal of building a regionally robust workflow. To do so, we trained local and regionally aggregated machine learning models using multiples EO sensors, including Planet SuperDove and Pléiades/Pléiades Neo. We found that regionally aggregated models often outperformed locally trained ones, and that leveraging higher temporal resolution sensors improved year-to-year consistency in predictions.

presentations.title: Floodplain Over Troubled Water: Mapping Daily Inundation Patterns In The Lowland Oder River Using Digital Elevation Models And Satellite Imagery
presentations.affiliation: Leibniz Institute of Freshwater Ecology and Inland Fisheries (IGB), Berlin
presentations.abstract: River basins are increasingly challenged by climatic extremes, altering the magnitude, frequency and duration of floods. To improve our understanding of floodplain dynamics, we derived daily patterns of flood duration and extent in the Oder floodplain. We integrated high-resolution digital elevation models (DEM) with the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) derived from Sentinel-2 imagery. A slope-corrected Relative Elevation Model (REM) was calculated for a 170-km river stretch to delineate areas of equal elevation above the river. Inundation patterns were mapped using daily gauge data from 2017-2022 and validated against NDWI-based inundation maps.

presentations.title: HYPERSPECTRAL REMOTE SENSING OF COUPLED WATER QUALITY VARIABLES OVER TIME AND SPACE ENABLES LAKE ECOSYSTEM UNDERSTANDING
presentations.abstract: Cutting-edge lake ecosystem monitoring needs multimodal data and will likely benefit from new information-rich satellite remote sensing technologies. The LakeView campaign aimed to capture such patterns with simultaneous airborne hyperspectral imaging and comprehensive in situ sampling of Lake Mendota in Madison, WI, USA. 14 sampling events in March through November, 2024 captured limnological conditions of the lake. Canonical correlation analyses reveal data clusters aligned with known phases of Lake Mendota's annual cycle. Partial least squares regression models unveil spectra-variable relationships and show significant predictive power for optical and non-optical variables over time and space.

presentations.title: HYDROLOGICAL VARIABILITY CONTROLS PRIMARY PRODUCTION AND METHANE EMISSIONS ACROSS TEMPORAL SCALES IN A MEDITERRANEAN RESERVOIR
presentations.abstract: Mediterranean reservoirs exhibit strong hydrological variability across seasonal, interannual, and synoptic time scales, driven by climate forcing and management practices. We combined satellite observations, inflow estimates, reservoir modelling, and in situ GHG-flux measurements to examine how hydrology and mixing dynamics regulate PP and CH4 emissions in a small (~20 hm3) eutrophic reservoir in southern Spain (Cubillas Reservoir). PP and CH4 emissions respond differently across temporal scales but are consistently modulated by hydrodynamic variability.

title: The Next Frontier in Aquatic Sciences: Linking Remote Sensing, Data Science, Modeling, and Open Science to Better Understand Aquatic Ecosystems

presentations.title: DEVELOPING AN INVENTORY OF NATURALLY OCCURRING PONDS IN KARST TERRAIN FROM LIDAR
presentations.abstract: Karst terrain, most commonly associated with areas underlain by carbonate rocks, makes up 15% of the Earth’s land surface. While karst landscape is well-known for its limited surface water storage and stream networks, karst ponds can develop naturally when karst depressions become blocked and filled with water. Limited studies have shown that karst ponds can serve important ecological functions; however, our understanding of the ecohydrological roles these ponds play at regional scales is very limited because few comprehensive karst pond inventories exist. Manually documenting the locations of karst ponds is a tedious task, complicated by the abundance of both natural sinkholes and anthropogenically created ponds. In this study, we developed a new semiautomated method that processes lidar intensity and elevation data to map naturally occurring karst ponds. The method separates natural ponds from man-made ponds using lidar-revealed microtopographic features. We applied this method to Hart County, Kentucky (USA), a pervasively karstified area within the Pennyroyal Karst Region. The semiautomated process identified 2,940 ponds in the county (160 km 2 ). Of these, the method identified 310 (10.5%) as naturally occurring ponds, with an average size of 1,174 m 2 . This semiautomated method provides an efficient way to inventory naturally occurring ponds in karst terrain. Mapping these karst ponds provides critical baseline data for future studies on land-use planning, hydrology, aquatic ecology, and landscape evolution in karst regions.

presentations.title: Evaluating algorithms to model productivity and clarity in optically complex Arctic lagoons.
presentations.abstract: The Arctic is undergoing environmental changes faster than the global average, with near coastal areas seeing some of the most profound changes. Coastal areas represent interfaces between terrestrial and marine ecosystems, where processes such as coastal erosion and permafrost thaw are rapidly changing ecosystem function. Arctic lagoons are uniquely valuable ecosystems, providing food for indigenous communities and linking land inputs to marine ecosystems. Access to these systems is limited by remote and harsh conditions. Remote sensing platforms can detect ocean color and apply algorithms to estimate concentrations of optically active substances at broad temporal and spatial scales. Current algorithms to convert from remote sensing output to ground level water chemistry values often perform poorly in arctic coastal waters due to the complex optical properties, driven by high CDOM and large gradients of suspended sediments. This study seeks to rectify this by analyzing the relationship between in situ hyperspectral ocean color measurements and optically active substances in an arctic lagoon. We continuously collected 240km of water chemistry and remote sensing reflectance measurements, ranging from freshwater to marine areas. Preliminary data shows current algorithms can be optimized to estimate optically active substances. Model optimization will combine our data, previously defined algorithms, and machine learning methods. After the accurate estimations of optically active substances, we will the use historical imagery to understand how these areas have changed.

presentations.title: GEOSPATIAL ASSESSMENT AND PREDICTION OF SPATIOTEMPORAL VARIABILITY OF DISSOLVED ORGANIC CARBON IN THE ADIRONDACK STATE PARK (NY USA)
presentations.abstract: Dissolved organic carbon (DOC) plays a significant role in lake biogeochemistry and the global carbon cycle. Long-term monitoring in the northeast United States, northern Europe, and elsewhere has revealed widespread DOC increases, a process known as “browning”, as it imparts a brownish hue to water. Since DOC regulates numerous lake dynamics and processes, understanding the spatiotemporal dynamics of browning is a critical research challenge. While long-term in-situ datasets provide critical site-specific information, their limited coverage leaves broader variability across space and time poorly characterized. Here, we use multi-sensor satellite data (Landsat 5-9 and Sentinel-2; 1984–2025) and geospatial analysis to characterize long-term increases in DOC concentrations in hundreds of previously unstudied lakes across the Adirondack State Park (New York, USA). We derive chromophoric dissolved organic matter (CDOM) from multi-decadal satellite reflectance, convert satellite-estimated CDOM to DOC using empirical relationships, and assess trends in browning across lakes. Our results highlight widespread increases in DOC across the park with substantial differences in rates between lakes, showing clear spatial gradients associated with historical acidification, ongoing recovery, and other forms of environmental change. Given DOC’s role in lake functioning, these ongoing changes are likely to impact lakes in multiple ways, thereby motivating efforts to develop predictive models to forecast lake browning under future environmental changes.

presentations.title: Linking PACE Hyperspectral Ocean Color with Underway Metaproteomics across Seasonal Transects in the Northwest Atlantic
presentations.abstract: Phytoplankton communities structure the marine ecosystem, yet connections between satellite-detected community patterns and the molecular processes shaping their physiology remain limited. We conducted two seasonal transects between Bermuda and Woods Hole (March and September 2025), collecting continuous underway particulate material for high-resolution, mass-spectrometry-based metaproteomics paired with collocated PACE hyperspectral ocean color observations. Together, these datasets capture contrasting ecological regimes: March conditions featured deeper mixing and elevated chlorophyll associated with early-spring blooms, whereas September conditions reflected strongly stratified, lower-biomass waters with distinct light–nutrient environments. By integrating taxon-resolved proteomic signatures with PACE-derived phytoplankton functional types, spectral traits, and size-class structure, we assessed how microbial community composition and physiological status shift across the Sargasso Sea, Gulf Stream, and shelf–slope system. Preliminary analyses reveal coherent transitions in both hyperspectral PFTs and proteomic indicators across hydrographic features, including taxon-specific nutrient stress responses that align with frontal boundaries and seasonal forcing. This approach demonstrates how hyperspectral satellite observations and molecular-level measurements can be jointly leveraged to diagnose phytoplankton ecological function at basin scales, offering a framework for interpreting PACE products across varying oceanographic and seasonal conditions.

presentations.title: Emergent land hypsographic constraints on hydrology and carbon cycle scaling in inland water networks
presentations.affiliation: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
presentations.abstract: Bottom-up scaling from local or regional studies is a common approach to studying carbon cycling in aquatic networks. Inland water networks are globally heterogeneous and dynamic systems, so models that reduce complexity and heterogeneity at network and larger scales are needed to reveal links between functioning and top down constraints. Earth’s hypsography imposes a top down constraint on the configuration and roles of these networks, but also on the distribution of soil carbon stocks along the elevation plane. Here, we test how heterogeneity at multiple scales can be reduced through aggregation using land hypsography. Hypsography is an efficient tool for factor reduction because previous studies have proven that fundamental hydrological properties scale with the hypsographic integral. Using open-access datasets, we map soil organic carbon, hydrological properties, and climate variables to hypsographic curves to determine emergent patterns over different spatial scales in the contiguous United States. We hypothesize that hydrologic, climatic, and SOC stocks will co-vary with hypsographic indices. From this method, we can build a framework that can be applied to aquatic networks globally and over deep time to infer first-order controls on the aquatic carbon cycle.

presentations.title: Arctic Cryospheric Change and Implications for Arctic Mobility
presentations.abstract: The Arctic is warming nearly four times faster than the global average, driving rapid changes in the cryosphere and altering mobility and safety for remote and predominantly Indigenous communities across the circumpolar north. Sea ice, lake ice, and snow are thinning, forming later, and disappearing earlier, reducing the reliability of ice roads, snowmobile trails, and traditional travel routes essential for resupply, subsistence, and social connection. Warmer, wetter winters are also degrading ice quality, increasing the prevalence of weak white ice that poses safety risks even when ice appears sufficiently thick. These changes heighten vulnerability to hazardous ice conditions, threatening livelihoods, food security, and cultural continuity. Here we present preliminary long-term trends in Arctic snow, lake ice, and sea ice from 1950–2024 using reanalysis datasets. The results identify regions most sensitive to cryospheric loss, providing a baseline for understanding how changing ice and snow conditions affect mobility across the Arctic. By integrating multiple components of the cryosphere, this work highlights emerging areas of risk for Indigenous and northern communities and supports efforts to plan for safer travel under increasingly unstable winter conditions.

presentations.title: Enhancing Remote Sensing of Riverine Total Phosphorus Concentrations by Incorporating Land Surface Temperature
presentations.abstract: Remote sensing has become an increasingly important tool for water quality monitoring; however, most existing approaches for retrieving non-optically active parameters remain constrained by their reliance on spectral characteristics alone. This study integrates land surface temperature (LST) with spectral features in a machine learning framework to improve the accuracy of total phosphorus (TP) concentration estimation in rivers. Focusing on the Dongjiang River, a subtropical river in China, we utilized multi-source data from Landsat 8 and Landsat 9 to construct a combined feature set comprising spectral reflectance and LST. Feature selection was conducted using Pearson correlation analysis and Random Forest feature importance to identify the most effective predictors for TP estimation. A regression model was then developed to examine the spatiotemporal dynamics of TP concentrations in the Dongjiang River’s main channel and delta from 2014 to 2024. The results revealed that: (1) the annual mean TP concentrations in the delta is higher than the river; (2) TP concentrations in the delta exhibited more pronounced seasonal fluctuations than those in the main channel; (3) the most influential predictors for TP estimation were a combination of the blue, green, and red spectral bands along with LST; and (4) models incorporating LST achieved significantly higher accuracy than those based solely on spectral reflectance, with improved R² and RMSE values across most TP concentration ranges (except for 0.04–0.06 mg/L). These findings demonstrate that integrating LST with spectral features substantially enhances the accuracy of remote sensing–based TP retrieval in rivers, offering new opportunities for improved large-scale water quality monitoring.

presentations.title: IS A NITROGEN-FOCUSED LAKE MANAGEMENT FEASIBLE?
presentations.abstract: The European Water Framework Directive requires that all European lakes eventually reach good ecological conditions. To fulfill this in Danish lakes, phosphorus (P) inputs are targeted as the main management strategy. However, for certain lakes, this is technically neither feasible nor sufficient. Further, recent studies have highlighted the potential for a nitrogen-focused (N) targeted management to improve water quality. We merged multiple open-access databases to create a dataset of water quality, land use, catchment characteristics and hydraulic connectivity for Danish lakes with which we evaluated if a management focusing on reductions of N, P, or both would be optimal to improve the ecological states of Danish lakes. We compared two nutrient limitation classification methods, stoichiometric balance and molar N to P ratios. We used conditional inference trees to partition the multivariate lake dataset, double machine learning to estimate the causal effect of improving lake conditions by either N or P reduction, and ordinal logistic regression to evaluate at which nutrient thresholds further N or P reduction is more important. Our results highlight that N-limited lakes are generally in worse ecological states than P- or co-limited lakes, that only co-limited lakes have a statistically significant probability of achieving a better ecological state by reducing N or P further, and that a management strategy on first reducing N and then P could potentially improve Danish lakes.

presentations.title: CONSEQUENCES OF CLIMATE REANALYSIS MODEL USE FOR ESTIMATES OF LAKE PRODUCTIVITY: INSIGHTS FROM THE GLOBAL LAKE METABOLISM REPOSITORY
presentations.abstract: In lake ecosystem models, the atmosphere is often designated as a driver of physical and biological processes. Estimates of metabolism that make use of free water dissolved oxygen techniques rely on accurate wind speed and irradiance data to estimate gas exchange and primary production, respectively. These meteorological data from a lake’s surface are not always available, leading many to use climate reanalysis products (e.g., ERA-5, NLDAS-2, NCEP) for time series imputation or as a replacement. However, the implications of model choice and the necessity for bias correction remains unclear. This issue is particularly important for the Global LAke Metabolism Repository (GLAMR), which harmonizes high-frequency dissolved oxygen measurements from lentic waterbodies worldwide to estimate ecosystem productivity. To evaluate the suitability of reanalysis products for metabolism estimation, we compiled meteorological observations collected from open-data lake observatories in the United States and compared them to multiple reanalysis models. We quantified the effect of climate model choice on observation accuracy, estimates of gas exchange, and estimates of ecosystem productivity. Developing an understanding of the downstream effects of climate reanalysis models is a key step towards improving our understanding of metabolism at broad spatial scales, particularly in data-sparse areas.

presentations.title: Mixing regimes of the world's lakes
presentations.abstract: Classifying lakes by mixing regime provides a framework for understanding their ecology, biogeochemistry, and impacts of global change. To assess and scale the climate warming impacts on lakes and to help focus mitigation efforts, it is imperative to know the current global distribution of lake mixing regimes. However, beyond a theorized schematic proposed by Lewis Jr. in 1983, we do not know how many lakes of each mixing regime there are in the world, nor how they are spatially distributed. Here, we present the first empirical assessment of the current global distribution and occurrences of mixing regimes for ~1.4 million lakes in the world that are ≥0.1 km 2 in surface area. Mixing regimes were derived with a deterministic, physically-based model from satellite-derived and re-analysis data (2013 – 2021) of lake-specific properties (surface temperature, ice cover, transparency, wind, solar radiation, and mean lake depth), presented in the novel LakeMIX dataset. LakeMIX fills a crucial spatial data gap in large-scale limnological research, especially for the incorporation of small lakes and understudied geographies of remote regions. The data are in an analysis-ready format and will be made openly available.

presentations.title: Determining Optimal Remote Sensing Sampling Frames for Global Lakes
presentations.abstract: Current limnological remote sensing studies face a foundational methodological challenge: what window size to use to represent a lake? Is it better to use spectral values extracted from windows of a fixed size, or best to tailor buffer sizes to the spectral and spatial characteristics of each? This choice is unstandardized, and any resulting impact on the values extracted for studies is largely unknown. Here, we address this problem with three new analyses and data sets that can standardize global lake observation. Part 1 is a massive geospatial dataset of tens of millions of observations from 1.4 million lakes (Landsat/Sentinel-2, multiple years). Data were extracted from multiple concentric buffers (e.g., 1m, 10m, ..., 250m) around HydroLAKES centroids, summarizing mean values across all bands. Part 2 is an automated methodology designed to determine the largest of these concentric circles composed entirely of water for each lake worldwide. Optimal buffer size is determined by finding the threshold at which the signal abruptly changes (water-land boundary). The search employs a recently developed tree-search platform that automatically writes algorithms to solve scorable data problems. Part 3 is a derived measure of internal water 'similarity', quantified by comparing band metrics obtained from the various water-only concentric rings. Together, this three-part approach provides data-informed optimal window sizes, a new thresholding algorithm, and a new multi-terabyte database of pre-computed observations, contributing to consistent, global limnological remote sensing.

presentations.title: Assessing the Contributions of Oil and Gas Exploitation to Mangrove Degradation in the Niger Delta: A Geospatial Assessment of Rivers State, Nigeria
presentations.abstract: Oil and gas expansion in the Niger Delta, Nigeria has intensified pressures on mangrove ecosystems. This study assessed the contributions of oil and gas exploitation to mangrove degradation in Rivers State, from 1986 to 2025. Spatial datasets representing pipelines, oil wells, gas fields, refineries, gas flare sites, etc. were analyzed. Min–max normalization and spatial joining were applied to derive an Oil and Gas Infrastructure Index for the 23 Local Government Areas. Landsat composites were classified into six land cover categories using a support vector machine (SVM) classification algorithm. Post-classification categorical change detection quantified mangrove transitions. Buffer and regression analyses examined proximity effects, while oil spill records (2007–2025) were overlaid with mangrove change and infrastructure intensity. A multi-criteria model identified restoration priority zones. Results show spatially concentrated infrastructure pressure, with intensity corridors in ONELGA, Okrika and Bonny. Mangrove extent declined from 2,518km² in 1986 to 2,192km² in 2025 (~325 km² loss), with dominant transitions from mangrove to waterbody and forest. The mangrove-to-waterbody conversions predominantly occurred in locations previously documented as oil spill sites in the region, indicating chronic spill-related degradation. Further, the buffer‐zone and regression analyses reveal an unexpected spatial relationship with greater mangrove loss occurring at larger distances from oil/gas infrastructure. Restoration priority zones were identified in sheltered creek systems.

presentations.title: The Effects of a Novel Aeration Device on Algae and Cyanobacteria Abundance
presentations.abstract: Eutrophication and hypoxia in inland water bodies due to human activities and internal nutrient loading continue to threaten freshwater ecosystems. Hypoxic conditions lead to fish kills, loss of diversity, and simplified food webs. Current eutrophication mitigation strategies have limitations that prevent their implementation in freshwater systems, particularly scalability to larger bodies of water. Aeration systems have been shown to be effective at reducing the effects of eutrophication, but current methods are not practical for implementation in large bodies of water. The purpose of this research is to determine whether a novel EMF aeration device, which has been deployed in 11 ponds and lakes, can be scaled to treat larger bodies of water, and whether it can reduce algae and cyanobacteria in lakes. Satellite imagery was used to quantify chlorophyll and phycocyanin in lakes before and after implementation of the aeration device at these locations as a means to quantify algae and cyanobacterial abundance. Algorithms for estimating chlorophyll were selected and calibrated against 141 lakes with reported chlorophyll values to identify the algorithm best suited for calculating chlorophyll in water bodies with differing optical properties. The NIR-Red algorithm was found to be best suited for estimating chlorophyll (R 2 = 0.229). Results indicated that the aeration device significantly reduced chlorophyll levels in the EMF treated bodies of water, t(10) = 2.979, p= 0.007 (one-tailed). Phycocyanin levels will also be determined in this study to assess efficacy of treatment.

presentations.title: LakeEnsemblR.WQ: An R Package for Ensemble Water Quality Modeling and System-Level Assessment of Lake Ecosystems
presentations.abstract: Aquatic ecosystems face increasing pressure from climate change and anthropogenic activities, necessitating more accurate and predictive modeling techniques to understand lake ecosystem processes and enable scenario testing. Although numerous lake models exist, setting up and operating them requires considerable expertise and time. Frameworks that facilitate the running and comparing different models are essential to address model uncertainty and provide a comprehensive view of lake ecosystem processes. The LakeEnsemblR package supports this need by allowing users to configure, execute and process multiple 1D hydrodynamic lake models within a single framework. To extend this capability, we have further developed the package LakeEnsemblR.WQ with a new framework that integrates water quality and biological modules for GLM-AED2, GOTM-WET and SELMAPROTBAS models. LakeEnsemblR.WQ aims to facilitate data preprocessing, calibration, post-processing, and also support the calculation of system metrics through concept, state, process, system framework. By integrating water quality modules and system-level validation metrics into a unified modeling platform, this package enhances the capacity to assess model uncertainty and improves the reliability of lake ecosystem predictions. The structure and workflow of LakeEnsemblR.WQ are demonstrated through its application to Lake Mendota, including cross-model comparisons and its utility for scenario analyses and system-level assessment.

presentations.title: Long-term Changes of Water Environments in Chinese Lakes via Integrated Remote Sensing and Data-Driven Models
presentations.affiliation: Nanjing Institute of Geography and Limnology, Chinese Academy of Sciences
presentations.abstract: Lakes act as sensitive sentinels of climate change and critical regulators of global biogeochemical cycles. However, monitoring their responses to climatic and anthropogenic stressors remains constrained by data gaps and the limitations of generalized models. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is currently catalyzing a paradigm shift in lake remote sensing, enabling high-precision retrievals driven by multi-source data. Leveraging MODIS, VIIRS, and OLCI satellite data, this study integrates novel deep learning architectures with long-term in-situ observations to develop robust water color parameter retrieval algorithms applicable from national to global scales, achieving accuracies exceeding 70%. Our analysis reveals a widespread decreasing trend in Total Suspended Matter (TSM) across Chinese lakes in the 21st century. Conversely, Chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) exhibits spatially divergent trends: Chl-a in the populous Eastern Plain lakes continues to rise. Collectively, these variations in water substances have induced a significant "Blue Shift" in lake color over the past 40 years: lakes on the Tibetan Plateau are becoming "bluer," while Eastern lakes are transitioning from yellow-green to green. We further disentangled the control mechanisms behind these shifts, highlighting strong spatial heterogeneity: climate change governs the environmental evolution of lakes in Western China, whereas anthropogenic activities dominate in the East. This research not only advances AI applications in limnology but also provides a critical data foundation and theoretical guidance for understanding lake ecosystem responses to dual climatic and human pressures.

presentations.title: PATTERNS AND DRIVERS OF CONTINENTAL-SCALE RESILIENCE IN LAKE SURFACE AREA
presentations.abstract: Lakes and reservoirs across the globe provide critical ecosystem services, and understanding the resilience of lake ecosystems in the context of changing climate and land cover is critical to preserving these resources. Past studies, generally focusing on water quality in northern temperate lakes, have shown that declines in resilience are tied to anthropogenic changes. Expanding our knowledge of the drivers of lake resilience beyond the regional scale, and to water quantity in addition to quality, has important implications for ecosystem processes at continental to global scales. Here we calculate long-term resilience in lake surface area across Australia (~17,000 lakes) and South America (~76,500 lakes) over 36 years. Patterns in resilience are highly spatially clustered within these two continents. We use machine learning to predict resilience across tens of thousands of lakes and identify the main drivers. Climatic variables, such as mean annual precipitation and temperature, explain the greatest amount of variability in resilience across both continents, but the relative importance of land cover variables differs between the two continents. Among land cover types, lakes with higher amounts of surrounding forest cover typically showed greater resilience than those in developed or barren areas. While the specific interactions between climate, land cover, and resilience vary between continents, our results indicate that ongoing deforestation, in addition to changes in precipitation and temperature, are likely to decrease lake resilience at a continental scale.
